Igniting Potential. Nurturing Character. Empowering Futures.
Welcome to Emmanuel Community School!
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to the website of Emmanuel Community School.
Established in 2012 as the first free school in the London Borough of Waltham Forest, we are proud to be sponsored by The Emmanuel School Trust (TEST) and to be recognised as a school with a strong Christian ethos.
At Emmanuel, we celebrate the uniqueness of every child. While our Christian values underpin all that we do, we are an inclusive school that warmly welcomes pupils of all faiths and none. Our mission is to nurture, challenge, and inspire each child to flourish both academically and personally.
We are committed to working in close partnership with parents, staff, and the wider community to ensure high standards are maintained and every child is empowered to reach their full potential. Following our most recent Ofsted inspection, we are more determined than ever to build on our strengths, fostering a culture of excellence, strengthening behaviour and pastoral support, and enhancing the quality of teaching and learning throughout the school.
At the heart of our vision is a dedication to transformational leadership and a learning environment where children feel valued, confident, and equipped for future success.
We invite you to explore our website to discover more about our values, curriculum, and community. Should you wish to experience the warm and welcoming atmosphere of our school first-hand, we would be delighted to arrange a visit. Please contact the school office on 020 8520 0775 to book an appointment.
Warmest regards,Mr Tayo FagbemiroHeadteacher

Who We Are
“With God all things are possible.”
Our Mission and Vision
Our Mission:
At Emmanuel Community School, we believe that the purpose of education is to empower and nurture every child to thrive and become the individuals God created them to be.
We strive to provide an environment where each student can experience the fullness of life, guided by Christian teachings and enriched by a strong Christian presence in mind, body and heart.
Our Vision:
A Community School serving the heart of Walthamstow guided by Christian teachings and principles.
Our Core Values
Our five core values underpin our work with the children. They are explored during assemblies and form a key part of our behaviour policy:
LOVE
JUSTICE
COURAGE
TRUTHFULNESS
FORGIVENESS
The school sees its provision for pupils in the area of spiritual, moral, social and cultural development as of paramount importance.
As part of its provision in this area, the school promotes the fundamental British values of:
Democracy
The Rule of Law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect
Our Story
The Emmanuel School Trust was established and incorporated as a company limited by guarantee in May 2011.
Following a successful bid to the Department for Education, the Trust opened the first Free School in the London Borough of Waltham Forest.
Emmanuel Community School (ECS) opened to new students in September 2012 in temporary premises (Emmanuel Christian Centre, Walthamstow) before moving to its permanent site, The Drive, in Walthamstow, a year later.
ECS was assessed by OFSTED as “A good school with outstanding Leadership” in 2014 and subsequently confirmed as “Good” in 2018.
In 2017, an inspection of the school’s distinctiveness as a Christian school (SIAMS section 48) rated it as ‘Outstanding in ALL areas.’
Our history is documented in the book, ‘Stepping Out On The Promise: From Vision to Reality: A journey towards excellent education in a Christian context’, available to purchase on Amazon here.

The Vision of the Trust
Our vision is to serve our local communities by providing excellent education rooted in the Christian Faith. (John 10:10b)
Guided by strong Christian principles, our ethos of ‘Learning for Life’ and high standards of literacy and numeracy as our key priorities. The range of subjects and learning opportunities we offer are well organised to capture and engage the interest and curiosity of children, ensuring they master basic skills and go on to excel at all levels.
We have a strong focus on creativity and optimise the use of indoor and outdoor spaces to enhance learning, with music and modern foreign languages playing a vital role in raising attainment. With an aspirational approach to pupil achievement, we firmly believe that demography must not determine destiny.
We are inspired by the outstanding achievements of Charter Schools in the USA which provide evidence of this. We use the “49 techniques that put students on the path to college” outlined by Doug Lemov in his book, “Teach like a Champion” as the bedrock of our teaching and learning. We use the freedoms associated with being an Academy Trust to better serve the needs of children.

Our Curriculum
Our curriculum is broad, balanced, relevant and stimulating, promoting curiosity and engagement from all.
At Emmanuel Community School, our aspiration is to enable the children to develop enquiring minds; we want them to have a love of learning and enjoy the sense of achievement they get when they ‘conquer’ a learning challenge.
We are proud to deliver the CUSP Curriculum—a vocabulary-rich, evidence-based framework designed to close learning gaps and raise standards for every child.
Rooted in research and professional collaboration, CUSP provides a carefully sequenced, knowledge-led approach across Reading, Writing, Science, History, Geography, and Art & Design. By explicitly teaching and revisiting key vocabulary and concepts, CUSP enables all pupils—including those with additional needs or learning English as an additional language—to access, articulate, and deepen their learning with confidence.

Pupil Premium and Sports Funding
Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium is additional funding given to schools so that they can support their disadvantaged pupils and close the attainment gap between them and their peers.
The government believes that the Pupil Premium, which is additional to main school funding, is the best way to address the current underlying inequalities between children, by ensuring that funding to tackle disadvantage reaches the pupils who need it most. The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011 and is allocated to schools to work with pupils who have been registered for free school meals at any point in the last six years (known as ‘Ever 6 FSM’). Schools also receive funding for children who are, or have been, looked after and for children of service personnel.
Schools have the freedom to spend the premium in the way they feel will best support the raising of attainment of the most vulnerable pupils. The aim is to support initiatives that ensure pupils reach their full potential, both academically and socially.
